title: Getting a SIM Card
short_description: A French SIM card helps you access mobile data, calls, SMS, and important verification services after arriving in France.
recommended_timing: Within your first few days in France
why_this_matters: You will need a French phone number for banking, deliveries, verification codes, and administrative services.

steps_summary.description: Compare prepaid or contract offers from operators such as Free Mobile, Orange, SFR, Bouygues Telecom, Lyca Mobile, or Lebara.

steps_summary.summary: Buy a SIM or eSIM with your passport
steps_summary.description: Buy in-store or online. Bring a valid passport (or national ID for EU students). Prepaid SIMs also require identity verification.
Insert the SIM or activate the eSIM, then keep your French number for banking and admin SMS codes.

warnings: Bring your passport when purchasing in-store.
Some providers may request proof of address.
Prepaid SIMs require ID verification under EU rules.

title: Finding Accommodation in France
short_description: Find and secure accommodation early — you need a signed lease (or equivalent) before applying for CAF housing aid.
recommended_timing: Before or immediately after arriving in France
why_this_matters: You need a valid accommodation contract before applying for CAF housing aid.

steps_summary.description: Check CROUS student housing, private rentals, and shared flats. Start early — demand is high at the start of the academic year.
Prefer viewing in person or via a trusted contact. Never pay a deposit before verifying the landlord and listing.

steps_summary.summary: Sign the rental agreement and pay the deposit
steps_summary.description: Keep a signed copy of the bail (lease) and inventory (état des lieux). You will need these for CAF.
Keep your lease and, if possible, a utility bill or landlord attestation — required for banking and admin steps.

warnings: Beware of housing scams — never send money before verifying the listing and landlord.
You need a valid lease (or CROUS attestation) before applying for CAF housing aid.
CAF housing aid is not retroactive: apply as soon as you have the keys.

title: Open an online bank account
short_description: Opening an online bank account is a crucial step for international students. It allows you to manage your finances and make payments.
recommended_timing: Before paying for visa validation or receiving money
why_this_matters: An online bank account allows you to pay visa-validation fees, receive money, and make transactions immediately while waiting for a traditional French bank account.

requirements.name: Visa or residence permit (non-EU; some apps accept it)
French address (often required for card delivery)

steps_summary.summary: Download the Application on your PlayStore(Android) or Appstore(IOS)
steps_summary.description:
Once installed, open the app and follow the on-screen steps.
Fill in the registration form by entering the required details

Upload a photo of an ID document — passport, national ID card, or visa (a residence permit may also be accepted depending on your country).
Take a selfie to confirm your identity.

steps_summary.summary: Receive IBAN and Order your Card
steps_summary.description: You can also create a free virtual card immediately to shop online while waiting for your physical card to arrive. Track the delivery on the application

warnings: Prepare your ID documents before you start.
An online IBAN is often enough to pay the visa-validation tax and receive transfers while you wait for a traditional bank.
Some landlords and employers still prefer a traditional French bank account.

title: Get a Navigo / Imagine R pass
short_description: Get unlimited public transport in Île-de-France (metro, bus, RER). Students under 26 living in the region can apply for the discounted Imagine R Étudiant annual pass.
recommended_timing: Within your first month in France
why_this_matters: Public transport is the main way to travel in Paris and Île-de-France. Imagine R (student) or Navigo Month/Week makes daily travel cheaper than buying single tickets.

requirements.name: Proof of identity (passport or ID card)
Proof of address in Île-de-France (for Imagine R)
Enrollment / school certificate for the current year (Imagine R Étudiant)
Recent ID photo (new Imagine R subscription)

steps_summary.description: Imagine R Étudiant: annual student pass if you are under 26 on 1 September, live in Île-de-France, and are enrolled in eligible studies. Otherwise use Navigo Month/Week (or Liber't) — available more broadly.

steps_summary.summary: Apply on Île-de-France Mobilités (or at a station desk)
steps_summary.description: For Imagine R, subscribe online at iledefrance-mobilites.fr. Upload your enrollment certificate (in French) and photo when asked.
Pay for the subscription, then collect or receive your Navigo card and load/activate the pass before travelling.

warnings: Imagine R Étudiant is for Île-de-France residents under 26 with a current-year enrollment certificate — outside Paris/IDF use local transport passes instead.
Travelling without a valid ticket can lead to a fine.

title: Validating your visa
short_description: Visa validation is required to activate your long-stay visa and legally stay in France as a student.
recommended_timing: Within your first 3 months in France
why_this_matters: Until you validate your VLS-TS online, it does not fully act as a residence permit. After 3 months without validation, you can lose the right to re-enter France freely and may be in an irregular situation.

steps_summary.summary: Go to the official visa validation website
steps_summary.description:
Use the French administration portal link below.
Click on the card "Je valide mon VLS-TS"

steps_summary.summary: Enter your visa number and personal details
steps_summary.description:
Enter your visa number and confirm it.
After confirmation, enter your date of beginning and end of validity, date of issue, reason for stay;

Enter the additional information: family circumstances, telephone number, email address; 
Indicate your date of arrival in France and your address in France;

Pay the stay tax shown on ANEF. For student VLS-TS, the reduced rate is €100 since 1 May 2026 (it was €50 before). Always confirm the amount displayed on the payment screen before paying — you can pay by card or with an electronic tax stamp (timbre fiscal).

You will receive two emails.

A first email with your login details. You will need it to access your account. It will contain the confirmation of the validation of your VLS-TS visa. 
 
A second email confirming the information you entered online. You can download the email of confirmation of the validation of your VLS-TS visa.

warnings: Validate within 3 months of your first entry into France (date stamped in your passport).
Fee amounts change: confirm the amount shown on ANEF before paying (student reduced rate €100 since 1 May 2026).
Keep the validation confirmation email/PDF — you will need it for banking, CAF, and health insurance.
You need a French address and a phone/email; a temporary address is acceptable to start.

official_links.label: Campus France — validating your long-stay visa

title: Open a Traditional Bank Account
short_description: Open a traditional French bank account to access long-term banking services, salary payments, and administrative processes.
why_this_matters: A traditional French bank account is often preferred for salary payments, rent direct debit, and some admin procedures, even if you already have an online IBAN.
steps_summary: Book an appointment online or in branch
warnings: Prepare your documents before booking an appointment.
Account approval may take several weeks.
Some banks require an in-person appointment.
Fees vary for student packages — ask about student offers.

title: Register for Public Health System
short_description: Register for French public health insurance (Assurance Maladie) via the dedicated foreign-student portal — affiliation is free and required for non-EU students.
recommended_timing: Within your first 1–2 months in France
why_this_matters: Without affiliation you generally pay full price for care and cannot get standard reimbursements. EU/EEA/Swiss students with a valid EHIC usually stay covered by their home system instead.

requirements.name: Student visa / validated VLS-TS or residence permit
Birth certificate / civil-status proof (often with translation)
Bank details / RIB (French or foreign IBAN accepted)

steps_summary.description: Use the Assurance Maladie portal for foreign students (not ameli.fr first). Enter your personal details and study start date.
Upload passport/ID, enrollment certificate, visa/residence proof, and civil-status documents (birth certificate). Non-EU students usually need a translation of the birth certificate.

steps_summary.summary: Get your provisional social security number
steps_summary.description: You receive a provisional number and temporary rights attestation. Keep them for care and reimbursement claims.

steps_summary.summary: Complete your file after visa validation
steps_summary.description: Once your VLS-TS is validated, upload the validated titre proof and your RIB to obtain a definitive social security number.
After you have a social security number, create your personal account on ameli.fr to track reimbursements and request a Carte Vitale.

warnings: Start on etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr — create an ameli.fr account only after you have a social security number.
Processing can take several weeks; keep your provisional attestation.
A foreign IBAN can be used for reimbursements if you do not yet have a French bank account.
EU/EEA/Swiss students with a valid European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) usually do not register on this portal.

title: Apply for CAF Housing Aid (CAF)
short_description: Apply for housing assistance from CAF after securing accommodation in France.
recommended_timing: As soon as you have the keys / move into your housing
why_this_matters: CAF housing aid (APL/ALS/ALF) can significantly reduce your rent. It is not retroactive — rights usually start the month after you apply and move in.

requirements.name: Signed rental contract (bail) or CROUS residency attestation
Landlord details (and SIRET if the landlord is a company)
Rent attestation (attestation de loyer) signed by the landlord
ID / visa or residence permit (as requested in your CAF file)

steps_summary.description: Visit the CAF website and start a new housing assistance application. Click on « Mes services en ligne/Faire une demande de prestation » and following the online instructions.
If you already have a CAF account, sign in and submit your application from your personal account.

Upload the documents CAF requests (lease, RIB, rent attestation, ID/residence proof, landlord SIRET if applicable) via your CAF account or the CAF mobile app. Respond quickly if more documents are asked.
Monitor your CAF account regularly to check whether additional documents or information are requested. Respond promptly to avoid delays.

After approval, CAF notifies you. Rights usually open the month after you move in and apply; first payment often arrives about 1–2 months later (e.g. move in September → rights in October → payment in November).

warnings: Housing aid is not retroactive — apply as soon as you have the keys.
You need a valid lease (or CROUS attestation) and a RIB before applying.
CAF processing can take several weeks; check your account for missing documents.
From 1 July 2026, eligibility rules tighten for some non-EU students — check caf.fr for your situation.

title: French Tax Declaration
short_description: If you are tax-resident in France and not attached to your parents' tax household, declare your income each spring on impots.gouv.fr (including a zero-income declaration when applicable).
recommended_timing: April–June each year for the previous calendar year (often after your first full year as a French tax resident)
why_this_matters: A tax return (or avis de non-imposition) is often needed for CAF, housing, and other admin. Declaring does not always mean you owe tax.

requirements.name: French tax number (numéro fiscal) if already assigned
Proof of income (payslips, etc.) if applicable

steps_summary.summary: Confirm you must file your own return
steps_summary.description: If you are under 25 and still studying, you may be attached to your parents' tax household instead of filing alone. Otherwise, file your own return if you are domiciled in France for tax purposes.

steps_summary.summary: Go to impots.gouv.fr and create / access your space
steps_summary.description: For a first declaration, create your personal tax account and follow the first-time filer flow.

Report wages, scholarships that are taxable, etc. Student job income may benefit from an exemption up to a yearly limit if you qualify — check the current amount on service-public.fr / etudiant.gouv.fr.

steps_summary.summary: Submit and download your tax notice
steps_summary.description: After processing, download your avis d'imposition or avis de non-imposition — keep it for CAF and other procedures.

warnings: Not every student must file alone: check whether you are attached to your parents' foyer fiscal.
If you file your own return, do it even with zero income so you can get an avis de non-imposition.
Missing the spring deadline can mean penalties or delays for benefits that ask for a tax notice.
Applies to EU and non-EU students who are French tax residents — not only non-EU visa holders.
